statement: For every connected locally finite almost transitive graph G with positive vertex Cheeger constant h(G), independent Bernoulli site percolation satisfies p_c(G)<p_u(G); this is Benjamini-Schramm (1996), Conjecture 6, and remains a conjecture in this row.

source.citation: Benjamini and Schramm, Percolation Beyond Z^d, Many Questions And a Few Answers, Electronic Communications in Probability 1 (1996), 71-82, Conjecture 6 and Section 2
source.location: PDF pp. 72-73, 76; lines 51-89, 256-260 in web extraction
source.quote: Assume that the almost transitive graph G has positive Cheeger constant. Then pc(G) <pu(G).

remaining_gap: The conjectured implication is unproved here; verify current status and separately audit any proposed proof.

statement: For iid Bernoulli bond percolation, disjoint finite x-y edge cuts F_1,...,F_n imply tau_p(x,y) <= product_i(1-(1-p)^|F_i|).

assumptions.cuts: each finite and separates x,y; pairwise edge-disjoint

proof_or_counterexample: Every connecting path meets each cut. The event that each cut has an open edge uses pairwise disjoint edge coordinates, hence independent; its probability is the displayed product.
remaining_gap: No gap in this lemma; applying it to random adaptive cuts requires a fresh-coordinate argument.

statement: For an infinite connected locally finite vertex-transitive graph with, for each n, n pairwise edge-disjoint o-y_n cuts of size at most fixed K, iid bond percolation has p_u=1.

assumptions.cuts: fixed K and n disjoint o-y_n cuts for every n

proof_or_counterexample: Under uniqueness at p<1, theta(p)>0. Harris association gives P(I_o and I_y)>=theta(p)^2, and uniqueness makes this a connection. L1 bounds connection by [1-(1-p)^K]^n -> 0; contradiction. At p=1 the connected infinite graph has one infinite cluster.
remaining_gap: Hypothesis is not implied by positive Cheeger constant.

statement: In a one-ended connected graph of max degree d and positive edge Cheeger constant h_E, at most d(|B_R(x)|+|B_R(y)|) pairwise disjoint x-y cuts can have size at most K, where R=ceil(K/h_E)+1.

assumptions.graph: one-ended, connected, locally finite, max degree d

proof_or_counterexample: Independently checked minimal-cut argument: every inclusion-minimal x-y cut has exactly x and y components; an extra component would make an incident cut edge inessential. One-endedness makes one endpoint component A finite, with |A|<=K/h_E. Its connected vertices lie within |A|-1 steps of x or y; all its cut edges touch the corresponding ball. Disjoint cuts consume distinct edges from at most d(|B_R(x)|+|B_R(y)|) such edges.
remaining_gap: This is an obstruction to L2 on the one-ended class, not a proof of p_c<p_u.

statement: On an infinite vertex-transitive locally finite connected graph with iid Bernoulli bond percolation, uniqueness and theta(p)>0 force tau_p(x,y)>=theta(p)^2 for all x,y, so the two-point kernel cannot be bounded on ell^2. If it is bounded for some p>p_c, then p_c<p_u.
proof_or_counterexample: Independent derivation: I_x and I_y are increasing tail events, so Harris via cylinder approximation gives P(I_x cap I_y)>=theta^2. Uniqueness makes the intersection a connection. For unit f_S=1_S/sqrt(|S|), <f_S,T_p f_S> >= |S|theta^2, unbounded as |S| grows. If T_p bounded, entrywise monotonicity under the uniform-label coupling bounds T_q for all q<=p; therefore no q<=p admits uniqueness, and the infimum p_u is >=p.
remaining_gap: No proof that some p>p_c has a bounded two-point operator on every nonamenable Cayley graph.

statement: The kernel K(i,j)=(1+|i-j|)^(-3/4) on Z has uniformly square-summable rows but is unbounded on ell^2; it is also symmetric, nonnegative, translation invariant and positive semidefinite.

assumptions.kernel: specified formula, generic kernel rather than fixed-p iid Bernoulli connection function

proof_or_counterexample: Row square sum is 1+2 sum_{m>=1}(1+m)^(-3/2)<=5. For f_n=1_{[1,n]}/sqrt(n), each of n^2 kernel entries is >=(1+n)^(-3/4), so <f_n,Kf_n>>=n(1+n)^(-3/4)->infinity. PSD follows independently because K(i,j)=E[e^{-|i-j|T}] for T Gamma(3/4,1), and the conditional one-dimensional percolation connectivity matrix is a sum of cluster-indicator rank-one matrices on finite support.
remaining_gap: This refutes only a generic operator inference; it does not refute C0047.

statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on the simple right Cayley graph of C_2*C_m with S={a,b,b^{-1}} and integer m>=3, p_c is the unique root in (0,1) of p[2 sum_{k=1}^{m-1}p^k-(m-1)p^m]=1, while p_u=1.
proof_or_counterexample: Right b-cosets form m-cycles. Contracting them yields a tree by free-product normal form. Entering a new cycle via an open a-bridge, the cycle-open component has size X and exactly X-1 unused outward a-bridges, independently open with p. Fresh block variables give iid offspring Binomial(X-1,p). Two disjoint arcs connect the entry to vertex k with probability p^k+p^{m-k}-p^m, so the offspring mean is the displayed polynomial. Standard bounded nondegenerate Galton-Watson survival gives the threshold. The a-bridges are singleton cuts; L2 gives p_u=1.
remaining_gap: This is a bond special case with infinitely many ends; no conclusion for general one-ended graphs or the original site model.

statement: For Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected d-regular vertex-transitive graph, with rho=||A/d|| on ell^2, p*d*rho<1 implies tau_p(x,y) <= (p*d*rho)^dist(x,y)/(1-p*d*rho); hence p_u>=1/(d*rho), and p_c<1/(d*rho) suffices for p_c<p_u.

assumptions.rho: operator norm of normalized adjacency A/d

source.related_primary: Benjamini-Schramm 1996 Theorem 4 has the site analogue with factor k

proof_or_counterexample: An open connection has a simple open path. For length n the union bound counts at most A^n(x,y) simple paths, while A^n(x,y)<=d^n rho^n; repeated-edge walks only enlarge the count, never get assigned path probability. Sum n>=dist. The resulting decay contradicts the theta^2 lower bound under uniqueness (w556 S1), so no uniqueness occurs below 1/(d*rho).
remaining_gap: The inequality p_c<1/(d*rho) is not known for every nonamenable Cayley graph and is false as a sufficient route in some easy classes; parent unresolved by this criterion.
